## Find the mean
By the empirical rule, 95% of values lie within $2\sigma$ of the mean, so the range is $\mu - 2\sigma$ to $\mu + 2\sigma$.
The mean is halfway between the ends of the range.
\mu &= \frac{147.9 + 178.7}{2}
&= \frac{326.6}{2}
&= 163.3
## Find the standard deviation
The top of the range is $\mu + 2\sigma$.
2\sigma &= 178.7 - 163.3
2\sigma &= 15.4
\sigma &= 7.7
ANSWER: \mu = 163.3 \text{ cm},\ \sigma = 7.7 \text{ cm}

## Plot each male as (height, arm span)
Height goes on the horizontal axis and arm span on the vertical axis.
The eight males are $(168, 169)$, $(147, 150)$, $(134, 121)$, $(177, 176)$, $(172, 170)$, $(160, 163)$, $(152, 151)$ and $(153, 151)$.
Mark each one as a filled dot at that position.
ANSWER: \text{Eight male points plotted}

## Judge the strength and direction from the scatter plot
The points rise from bottom left to top right, so the correlation is positive. This rules out $-0.6$.
They lie close to a straight line, so the correlation is strong. This rules out $0.2$.
So $0.9$ is the best choice.
ANSWER: 0.9

## Say what 0.9 means in context
There is a strong positive linear relationship between height and arm span.
Taller people are very likely to have a longer arm span.
ANSWER: \text{Strong positive linear relationship}

## Draw arcs from A
Set the compass to more than half of $|AC|$.
With the point on $A$, draw one arc above $AC$ and one below it.
## Draw arcs from C
Keep the same compass setting. With the point on $C$, draw arcs that cross the first two.
## Join the crossing points
Draw a straight line through the two crossing points. This is the perpendicular bisector of $[AC]$ and it cuts $[AC]$ at its midpoint at $90^\circ$.
ANSWER: \text{Perpendicular bisector of } [AC] \text{ constructed}

## Use the bisector of [AC] from part (i)
The circumcentre is the point equally far from $A$, $B$ and $C$. It lies on the perpendicular bisector of every side.
## Construct the perpendicular bisector of [AB]
With the compass on $A$, then on $B$, using the same setting (more than half of $|AB|$), draw crossing arcs above and below $AB$.
Join the crossing points with a straight line.
## Mark the circumcentre
The two bisectors cross at a point $O$. This is the circumcentre.
## Draw the circumcircle
Put the compass point on $O$ and open it to reach $A$.
Draw the circle. It passes through $A$, $B$ and $C$.
ANSWER: \text{Circumcircle: centre } O,\ \text{radius } |OA|

## Multiply the side by the scale factor
|QR| &= k \times |EF|
&= 2.5 \times 3
&= 7.5
ANSWER: |QR| = 7.5 \text{ cm}

## Areas change by the scale factor squared
Lengths are multiplied by $k$, so areas are multiplied by $k^2$.
\text{Area } PQR &= k^2 \times \text{Area } DEF
18.75 &= 2.5^2 \times \text{Area } DEF
18.75 &= 6.25 \times \text{Area } DEF
## Divide both sides by 6.25
\text{Area } DEF &= \frac{18.75}{6.25}
&= 3
ANSWER: \text{Area } DEF = 3 \text{ cm}^2

## Check the class widths
Every age group is 10 years wide, so the height of each bar is just the percentage.
## Draw one bar for each group
Bars touch each other (no gaps) because the groups run on from one another.
Heights: $15$–$25$ is $24$, $25$–$35$ is $27$, $35$–$45$ is $25$, $45$–$55$ is $16$, $55$–$65$ is $8$.
ANSWER: \text{Bars of height } 24,\ 27,\ 25,\ 16,\ 8

## Add the percentages for ages 25 to 55
\text{Percentage} &= 27 + 25 + 16
&= 68
## Find 68% of 1000
\text{People} &= \frac{68}{100} \times 1000
&= 680
ANSWER: 680 \text{ people}

## The median is at the 50% mark
Add up the percentages from the youngest group until the total passes 50.
24 &< 50
24 + 27 &= 51
51 &> 50
The 50% mark is reached in the second group.
ANSWER: 25 \text{ to } 35 \text{ age group}

## Find the mid-interval value of each group
Mid-value = (lower end + upper end) $\div 2$.
\frac{15 + 25}{2} &= 20
\frac{25 + 35}{2} &= 30
\frac{35 + 45}{2} &= 40
\frac{45 + 55}{2} &= 50
\frac{55 + 65}{2} &= 60
## Multiply each mid-value by its percentage and add
The percentages add to 100, so divide the total by 100.
\text{Mean} &= \frac{(24 \times 20) + (27 \times 30) + (25 \times 40) + (16 \times 50) + (8 \times 60)}{100}
&= \frac{480 + 810 + 1000 + 800 + 480}{100}
&= \frac{3570}{100}
&= 35.7
ANSWER: 35.7 \text{ years}

## Use the margin of error formula
\text{Margin of error} &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{540}}
&= 0.043
## Write it as a percentage
\text{Margin of error} &= 0.043 \times 100
&= 4.3\%
ANSWER: 4.3\%

## Find the sample proportion
\hat{p} &= \frac{372}{540}
&= 0.6889
&= 68.9\%
## Subtract and add the margin of error
\text{Lower} &= 68.9 - 4.3
&= 64.6
\text{Upper} &= 68.9 + 4.3
&= 73.2
ANSWER: [64.6\%,\ 73.2\%]

## State the hypotheses
The null hypothesis says nothing has changed from 65%.
H_0: p &= 65\%
H_1: p &\ne 65\%
## Compare 65% with the confidence interval
65 &\in [64.6,\ 73.2]
65% lies inside the 95% interval, so there is not enough evidence to reject $H_0$.
Conclusion: at the 5% level of significance, the Netflix share of the market has not changed.
ANSWER: \text{Fail to reject } H_0: \text{ the Netflix share has not changed}

## Find the width of the lake at each line
Add the length above [PQ] to the length below it. Lines are $10$ m apart, from $P$ to $Q$ ($60$ m).
y_0 &= 0 + 10 = 10
y_1 &= 20 + 20 = 40
y_2 &= 10 + 20 = 30
y_3 &= 30 + 20 = 50
y_4 &= 30 + 10 = 40
y_5 &= 20 + 20 = 40
y_6 &= 0 + 0 = 0
## Add the middle widths
y_1 + y_2 + y_3 + y_4 + y_5 &= 40 + 30 + 50 + 40 + 40
&= 200
## Write down the Trapezoidal Rule
$A = \frac{h}{2}\left[(\text{first} + \text{last}) + 2(\text{sum of the rest})\right]$ with $h = 10$.
A &= \frac{10}{2}\left[(10 + 0) + 2(200)\right]
&= 5\left[10 + 400\right]
&= 5(410)
&= 2050
ANSWER: 2050 \text{ m}^2

## Volume = surface area x depth
V &= 2050 \times 8
&= 16400
ANSWER: 16400 \text{ m}^3

## Substitute r = 21 into the hemisphere formula
V &= \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3
&= \frac{2}{3}\pi (21)^3
&= \frac{2}{3}\pi (9261)
&= 6174\pi
ANSWER: 6174\pi \text{ cm}^3

## Set the cone volume equal to the hemisphere volume
The cone has radius $21$ and height $h_c$.
\frac{1}{3}\pi (21)^2 h_c &= 6174\pi
\frac{1}{3}\pi (441) h_c &= 6174\pi
147\pi h_c &= 6174\pi
## Divide both sides by 147 pi
h_c &= \frac{6174\pi}{147\pi}
&= 42
## Add the height of the hemisphere
The hemisphere is $21$ cm deep (its radius).
h &= 42 + 21
&= 63
ANSWER: h = 63 \text{ cm}

## Use the cosine rule for the angle opposite 60 m
Let $A = |\angle QBP|$, opposite the side of $60$ m.
60^2 &= 26^2 + 43^2 - 2(26)(43)\cos A
## Evaluate the squares and the product
3600 &= 676 + 1849 - 2236\cos A
3600 &= 2525 - 2236\cos A
## Isolate cos A
2236\cos A &= 2525 - 3600
2236\cos A &= -1075
\cos A &= -\frac{1075}{2236}
&= -\frac{25}{52}
## Take the inverse cosine
Use degree mode on the calculator.
A &= \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{25}{52}\right)
&= 118.74^\circ
ANSWER: |\angle QBP| = 118.74^\circ

## Find where L is on the runway
$L$ is $1250$ m from $S$. Change this to units.
\frac{1250}{250} &= 5
## Plot L and draw the flight path
Mark $L$ on the runway $5$ units from $S$ (half way).
At $L$, use a protractor to draw a line $14^\circ$ above the runway, going towards $E$. Stop it directly above $E$.
ANSWER: L \text{ is 5 units from } S

## Find the length of the arc
Arc length $= 2\pi r \times \frac{\theta}{360}$ with $r = 10$ and $\theta = 70$.
l &= 2\pi(10)\left(\frac{70}{360}\right)
&= 12.217
## Add the two straight 10 km legs
\text{Total} &= 10 + 10 + 12.217
&= 32.217
&= 32.22
ANSWER: 32.22 \text{ km}

## Read the co-ordinates of T
In $(x, y) = (-2, -5)$, the first number is the $x$-value: $2$ units to the left of the origin.
The second number is the $y$-value: $5$ units down.
Mark the point where these meet and label it $T$.
ANSWER: T(-2, -5) \text{ plotted}

## Equation of the line through A(3, -5) with slope -1
y - y_1 &= m(x - x_1)
y - (-5) &= -1(x - 3)
y + 5 &= -x + 3
x + y &= -2
## Equation of the line through B(6, 4) with slope 0
y - 4 &= 0(x - 6)
y &= 4
## Find where the lines meet
Put $y = 4$ into $x + y = -2$.
x + 4 &= -2
x &= -6
## Draw the lines
Draw $y = 4$ (horizontal through $B$) and $x + y = -2$ (through $A$, going up to the left). They cross at $F$.
ANSWER: F = (-6, 4)

## Use the distance formula for P(2, m) and B(6, 4)
\sqrt{(6 - 2)^2 + (4 - m)^2} &= \sqrt{41}
\sqrt{16 + (m - 4)^2} &= \sqrt{41}
## Square both sides and expand
16 + (m - 4)^2 &= 41
16 + m^2 - 8m + 16 &= 41
m^2 - 8m - 9 &= 0
## Factorise and solve
(m + 1)(m - 9) &= 0
m &= -1 \text{ or } m = 9
$P$ is below the $x$-axis, so $m$ is negative. Reject $m = 9$.
## Plot P
$P(2, -1)$ is $2$ across and $1$ down.
ANSWER: m = -1,\ P(2, -1)

## Substitute x = -2 and y = -5 into x - y - 3
x - y - 3 &= (-2) - (-5) - 3
&= -2 + 5 - 3
&= 0
The left side equals $0$, so $T$ is on $k$.
ANSWER: T \in k

## Pick a value for x and find y
Choose $x = 1$ and put it into $x - y - 3 = 0$.
1 - y - 3 &= 0
-y - 2 &= 0
y &= -2
ANSWER: (1, -2) \in k

## Find the slope of k
x - y - 3 &= 0
y &= x - 3
The slope of $k$ is $1$. Parallel lines have equal slopes, so the slope of $l$ is $1$.
## Find l through C(-3, 2) with slope 1
y - y_1 &= m(x - x_1)
y - 2 &= 1(x - (-3))
y - 2 &= x + 3
y &= x + 5
ANSWER: y = x + 5

## Use the discriminant for exactly one solution
Exactly one solution means the discriminant is zero.
b^2 - 4ac &= 0
## Substitute a = 3, b = -m, c = 3
(-m)^2 - 4(3)(3) &= 0
m^2 - 36 &= 0
## Solve for m
m^2 &= 36
m &= \pm 6
ANSWER: m = 6 \text{ or } m = -6

## A square is never negative
For every real $x$, a squared number is at least $0$.
(2x+3)^2 &\ge 0
## Add 7 to both sides
(2x+3)^2 + 7 &\ge 7
&> 0
## Conclude
The left-hand side is always greater than $0$, so it can never equal $0$. There are no real solutions.
ANSWER: (2x+3)^2 + 7 \ge 7 > 0 \text{, so there are no real solutions}

## (i) Substitute x = -1
3(-1)^2 + 2(-1) + 5 &= 3(1) - 2 + 5
&= 3 - 2 + 5
&= 6
Since $6 \ne 0$, $x = -1$ is not a solution.
## (ii) Expand the product
(x+1)(ax+b) + c &= ax^2 + bx + ax + b + c
&= ax^2 + (a+b)x + b + c
## Equate to 3x^2 + 2x + 5
ax^2 + (a+b)x + (b+c) &= 3x^2 + 2x + 5
Compare coefficients of $x^2$, $x$ and the constants.
## Coefficient of x^2
a &= 3
## Coefficient of x
a + b &= 2
3 + b &= 2
b &= -1
## Constant term
b + c &= 5
-1 + c &= 5
c &= 6
ANSWER: c = 6

## Integrate each term
Raise the power by 1 and divide by the new power: $\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + c$.
\int (2x^2 + 5x + 6)\,dx &= \int 2x^2\,dx + \int 5x\,dx + \int 6\,dx
&= \frac{2x^3}{3} + \frac{5x^2}{2} + 6x + c
ANSWER: \frac{2x^3}{3} + \frac{5x^2}{2} + 6x + c

## Write the area as an integral
Region $K$ lies between $x = 0$ and $x = 2$.
\int_0^2 (ax^2 + bx + c)\,dx &= 538
## Integrate each term
\left[\frac{ax^3}{3} + \frac{bx^2}{2} + cx\right]_0^2 &= 538
## Substitute the limits
At $x = 0$ every term is $0$, so only $x = 2$ matters.
\frac{a(2^3)}{3} + \frac{b(2^2)}{2} + c(2) &= 538
\frac{8a}{3} + 2b + 2c &= 538
## Simplify to the given equation
8a + 6b + 6c &= 1614
4a + 3b + 3c &= 807
ANSWER: 4a + 3b + 3c = 807

## Substitute z = 6 + 2i
z - iz &= (6 + 2i) - i(6 + 2i)
&= 6 + 2i - 6i - 2i^2
## Use i^2 = -1 and collect terms
z - iz &= 6 + 2i - 6i + 2
&= 8 - 4i
ANSWER: z - iz = 8 - 4i

## Find the modulus r
The point $\sqrt{3} - i$ has real part $\sqrt{3}$ and imaginary part $-1$.
r &= \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 + (-1)^2}
&= \sqrt{3 + 1}
&= \sqrt{4}
&= 2
## Find the argument
The point is in the fourth quadrant, so measure the reference angle and subtract it from $360^\circ$.
\tan A &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}
A &= 30^\circ
\theta &= 360^\circ - 30^\circ
&= 330^\circ
## Write in polar form
\sqrt{3} - i &= 2(\cos 330^\circ + i\sin 330^\circ)
## Apply de Moivre's Theorem
$[r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)]^n = r^n(\cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta)$.
(\sqrt{3} - i)^9 &= 2^9\left(\cos(9 \times 330^\circ) + i\sin(9 \times 330^\circ)\right)
&= 512(\cos 2970^\circ + i\sin 2970^\circ)
## Reduce the angle and evaluate
$2970^\circ - 8 \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ$, so $\cos 2970^\circ = 0$ and $\sin 2970^\circ = 1$.
&= 512(\cos 90^\circ + i\sin 90^\circ)
&= 512(0 + i(1))
&= 0 + 512i
## Read off a and b
a &= 0
b &= 512
ANSWER: a = 0,\; b = 512

## Set the two common differences equal
In an arithmetic sequence $T_2 - T_1 = T_3 - T_2$.
13 - 5e^{-k} &= 5e^{k} - 13
## Replace e^k with y
Since $y = e^k$, we have $e^{-k} = \dfrac{1}{y}$.
13 - \frac{5}{y} &= 5y - 13
## Multiply every term by y
13y - 5 &= 5y^2 - 13y
## Collect all terms on one side
0 &= 5y^2 - 13y - 13y + 5
0 &= 5y^2 - 26y + 5
ANSWER: 5y^2 - 26y + 5 = 0

## Factorise the quadratic in y
5y^2 - 26y + 5 &= 0
(y - 5)(5y - 1) &= 0
## Set each factor equal to zero
y - 5 &= 0 \quad \text{or} \quad 5y - 1 = 0
y &= 5 \quad \text{or} \quad y = \frac{1}{5}
## Replace y with e^k
e^k &= 5 \quad \text{or} \quad e^k = \frac{1}{5}
## Take natural logs to solve for k
k &= \ln 5 \quad \text{or} \quad k = \ln \frac{1}{5}
Write $\frac{1}{5} = 5^{-1}$ and use $\ln(a^b) = b\ln a$.
k &= \ln 5 \quad \text{or} \quad k = -\ln 5
ANSWER: k = \ln 5 \ \text{or} \ k = -\ln 5
